Request to Medical Affairs

Membrane evidence request

The CI Desk evidence library currently holds no references at all for Jason membrane, collprotect, permamem or the NOVAMag membrane. Its science desk is built to refuse to cite what it does not have, so today it answers every membrane question with "I have no reference for that". This is the list that fixes it, ordered by what the field needs first.

botiss CI Desk · evidence library gap analysis · 42 literature entries loaded, 0 on membranes

Why
The grafting range is now covered: 42 approved references across cerabone, cerabone plus, maxgraft and maxresorb, extracted from the training decks. The membrane range has nothing, because the membrane decks were not in that set. Everything below is a request for published references — a reprint, a citation list or a DOI is enough. We do not need the brochures.

Priority 1 — claims the field is already exposed on

These are the questions a periodontist asks in the room. Without a reference, a rep either says nothing or improvises, and improvising is what we are trying to stop.

Barrier duration, with the method used to measure it

Tier 2P1
Jason membrane · collprotect
The claim
"Jason gives a long barrier function; collprotect integrates faster." The indication split between the two rests entirely on this.
What we need
The barrier-duration figure for each membrane and how it was determined — histological degradation in vivo, in vitro enzymatic assay, or clinical observation. The number alone is not usable; a reviewer will ask the method immediately.
Why it is urgent
This is the most common membrane overclaim in the industry ("longer is better"). We want reps armed with the trade-off rather than the slogan.

Exposure and complication rates for each membrane

Tier 3P1
Jason membrane · collprotect · permamem
The claim
None yet — and that is the problem. Exposure is the practical driver of GBR failure, so it is the first thing a surgeon raises.
What we need
Any study reporting membrane exposure, dehiscence or complication rate for our membranes, with the number of cases and the follow-up. Studies with a comparator are far more valuable, but uncontrolled rates are still worth having.
Note
We will not turn this into a lower-exposure-than-competitor claim. Technique dominates the outcome and that would be tier 4. We want it so reps can answer the question honestly.

All NOVAMag membrane clinical data, with follow-up durations

Tier 3P1
NOVAMag membrane
The claim
"It resorbs, so no removal surgery." The mechanism is safe; everything past it is not.
What we need
Every clinical publication, each with its patient number and follow-up. Separately: the degradation timeline, and how gas formation is characterised and managed.
Why it is urgent
Highest overclaim risk in the portfolio: a young evidence base meeting the most enthusiastic audience. The surgeons most interested in magnesium are the ones who will read the papers. Currently the library holds one in-vitro-plus-two-patient report, and it addresses compatibility with our grafts, not efficacy.

Priority 2 — the range's own logic

Evidence that lets us explain why the range has four membranes instead of one.

Clinical publications on Jason membrane, sorted by design

Tier 3P2
Jason membrane
What we need
The complete publication list, grouped by design: systematic reviews, RCTs, cohorts, case series, preclinical. Plus, honestly, a map of where the gaps sit against Bio-Gide.
Why
Reps need to know what we can and cannot match. Claiming a comparable evidence base to Bio-Gide when we cannot loses the room permanently.

Clinical evidence for collprotect, and anything comparing it with Jason

Tier 3P2
collprotect
What we need
Publications on collprotect specifically, and any study putting the two side by side.
Why
The two are sold as an indication-matched pair. Without evidence for the split, reps default to treating them as interchangeable, which wastes the distinction we built the range on.

Validated exposed-healing protocols for permamem

Tier 1 / 3P2
permamem
What we need
Which open-healing protocols permamem is validated for, the recommended in-situ duration, and the evidence behind removal timing. Part of this is IFU and technical file rather than literature — both are useful.
Why
Intentional exposure is the reason to choose dPTFE at all. Reps need the protocol boundaries, not a general statement that dense PTFE tolerates exposure.

Cross-linking position

Tier 2P2
Jason membrane · collprotect
What we need
Our scientific position on native versus chemically cross-linked collagen, with the references behind it.
Why
Both our collagen membranes are native. That is a real differentiator against cross-linked competitors — but only if a rep can explain the trade-off rather than assert it.

Priority 3 — useful, not blocking

Head-to-head studies against Bio-Gide or Cytoplast

Tier 4P3
any membrane
What we need
Any direct comparison, with the endpoint and the comparator's exact product name.
Handling
Tier 4, so nothing here becomes a spoken superiority claim without regulatory sign-off. We want it recorded so the desk can tell a rep what does and does not exist, instead of leaving them to guess.

Membrane plus graft combination data

Tier 3P3
Jason + cerabone · permamem + cerabone plus · NOVAMag + cerabone plus
What we need
Studies on the combinations the field actually uses, since almost every case pairs a membrane with a graft.
Note
The library already holds the NOVAMag plus cerabone plus compatibility report. A combination study supports a claim about the combination, never about either component alone — the desk enforces this, so combination papers do not fill single-product gaps.

What helps, and what does not

Send

  • PDFs of published papers, in any quantity — there is a pipeline for bulk import
  • A plain citation list, or just DOIs
  • IFU and technical-file extracts for dimensions, durations and handling
  • Validation reports, clearly labelled as such
  • An honest note where evidence does not exist yet

Do not bother sending

  • Brochures and sales decks — useful for tier 1 facts, but they are not citable evidence and we already have the grafting set
  • Case documentation already in the decks: 29 documented cases are loaded, at the lowest tier
  • Any figure without its endpoint, sample size and follow-up — it cannot be scoped, so it cannot be used
  • Claims text without the underlying reference

How each reference gets recorded

So you know what happens to what you send, and why the scope statement matters more than the citation.

  1. Bibliographic fields — title, authors, journal, year, DOI or PMID — are extracted mechanically and checked against the page.
  2. Study design and which product was actually studied are recorded separately. This second field matters most: most classic xenograft literature was generated on Bio-Oss, and the two get conflated constantly.
  3. What the reference licenses is written by hand, stated narrowly. If the endpoint was radiographic ridge width at six months, that is what it says — not "volume stability".
  4. Who verified it is recorded. Until someone confirms the paper says what it is cited for, the desk flags it on every citation.
Note
Nothing in the library was generated. Every reference came from a citation printed in an approved botiss deck. Where a source is not clinical evidence it is labelled — the 156-clinician handling survey, the Eurofins validation report, the trade-journal figures, the deck case documentation. Approval makes a citation usable; it does not change what the source is.
Generated from the botiss CI Desk evidence library. Claim tiers: 1 portfolio fact · 2 mechanism or preclinical · 3 clinical outcome for our product · 4 comparison with a named competitor. Tier 3 needs a library reference and sign-off; tier 4 should be assumed unsayable until regulatory clears it. This document is an internal evidence request, not a claims approval, and not clinical or regulatory advice.
